text:
maria: Quick PSA — saw a customer integration where the Node SDK fires duplicate user actions after a token refresh when upstream returns 429. Repro is pretty consistent in our staging.
maria: Steps: 1) long-running request streaming -> token expires mid-request 2) SDK triggers refresh, while request retry logic also replays the request 3) upstream 429 + retries cause duplicate processing on server side
maria: log snippet:
```
[2026-03-22T15:02:13Z] req_id=abc123 POST /v1/generate body_len=512 -> 401 token_expired
[2026-03-22T15:02:13Z] token -> refreshing (started)
[2026-03-22T15:02:14Z] req_id=abc123 POST /v1/generate RETRY attempt=1
[2026-03-22T15:02:15Z] req_id=abc123 POST /v1/generate RETRY attempt=2 -> 429
```
maria: Main issue: simultaneous refresh + retry code paths cause >1 outgoing request for the same logical client operation. We need an approach that avoids unsafe replays without breaking streaming semantics.
alex: Can you paste SDK version and whether this is default retry/backoff? Also which language (Node/Python)?
maria: Node SDK v0.8.2, default retry enabled. Repro also seen in a customer using our hosted API but server-side doesn't dedupe these requests.
david: Two orthogonal fixes I see: 1) client-side idempotency keys (idempotency-key header) + short TTL server dedupe 2) avoid double-send by singleflight-ing refresh + request replay — i.e., when refresh is in flight, queue subsequent requests until token replaced.
ken: I vote both. Idempotency keys are safer but we've seen customers not setting them. We should add a default idempotency behavior in SDK where feasible (for non-streaming RPCs) and a small in-process dedupe cache keyed by (operation, body-hash, idempotency-key) with TTL ~30s.
sasha: For retries/backoff, add full-jitter exponential backoff. Example (Node) we can copy into SDK:
```
// full jitter: sleep = rand_between(0, base * 2^attempt)
function backoffMs(attempt, base = 100) {
  const cap = 10000;
  const t = Math.min(base * Math.pow(2, attempt), cap);
  return Math.floor(Math.random() * t);
}
```
sasha: Also add a quick circuit-breaker on 429 bursts to stop aggressive replay when upstream overloaded.
alex: Parity ask: we need identical default dedupe + idempotency behavior across Node/Python/Go. I'll sketch an API: SDK auto-adds X-Redwood-Idempotency for idempotent endpoints unless user passes their own header. For streaming endpoints we skip auto-idempotency and instead rely on singleflight refresh + resume tokens.
maria: For token refresh: implement a single in-flight promise per client instance: when refresh starts, other requests should await it (or return a polite 429->retry path) instead of firing their own refreshes. This prevents N refresh races.
david: +1. Implementation hint: per-client 'refreshLock' Promise that is set while pending. On 401: if refreshLock exists await it, else create and run refresh, then resolve lock.
ken: What about long-poll / streaming where awaiting refresh would block too long? Maybe allow streaming to attach a detached retry strategy: emit "auth_lost" event to app so they can checkpoint/resume if they want full control.
alex: I'll open a single PR that touches node + python: 1) singleflight refresh, 2) small in-memory dedupe map for non-stream requests, 3) add X-Redwood-Idempotency default header, 4) jittered backoff implementation and circuit breaker metric.
maria: Can you also add sample app in examples/ that demonstrates unsafe-replay and the fix? We can use it for onboarding and regression tests.
alex: Yep. ETA: PR draft tomorrow, full review by end of week. I'll tag @ken @david for arch review.
sasha: Suggest telemetry: emit metrics retry_count, duplicate_detected, token_refresh_races, idempotency_hits. That will help us tune TTL and backoffs.
maria: Agree. Also log a lightweight event when we auto-add an idempotency header (so apps know we did it).
ci-bot: deploy-bot: CI pipeline triggered for alex/new-dedupe-work (build #482)
alex: Thanks — will add unit tests + e2e staging scenario. If anyone has objections to the default idempotency header, speak now.
ken: No objections. :thumbsup:
david: No objections.
maria: Cool. I'll create a troubleshooting blurb for support: how to disable auto-idempotency and recommended server-side dedupe config.
maria: Action items recap:
- alex: PR implementing singleflight refresh + dedupe + jittered backoff + examples (due EOW)
- sasha: add circuit-breaker + metric names (this week)
- ken/david: review arch + server-side dedupe guidance
- maria: support doc + staging regression test
maria: Thanks everyone :rocket:
